newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian 88 expects probe to come up dry.
newsitem.headline: Canadian 88 expects probe to come up dry.

text.p: Greg Noval, chief executive of Canadian 88 Energy Corp, said on Tuesday he was confident that an investigation launched into West Central Capital Corp 's trading in Morrison Petroleums Ltd stock would find no evidence of impropriety.
Noval also said his firm's shareholders would take in most of the profits generated from a sale of Morrison stock by West Central if Canadian 88's takeover bid for Morrison fails to be the highest.
"Canadian 88 shareholders get two-thirds of any trading profits that West Central may generate," Noval said in an interview from Toronto.
"And they don't have any of the downside -- it's a pretty good deal for 88 shareholders."

Trades in Morrison stock made by West Central in the days leading up to Canadian 88's C$652-million takeover bid for Morrison earlier this month are the subject of a probe being launched by the Alberta and Ontario securities commissions.
In its offering document to Morrison shareholders, Canadian 88 listed C$44 million worth of trades in the target firm's stock made by West Central, a private firm owned by a Calgary lawyer.

The activity resulted in West Central owning eight percent of Morrison shares, which has been pledged to Canadian 88's bid. West Central was the firm that had requested Morrison's shareholder list prior to the offer.

The securities regulators have said they would investigate whether the trades involved a practice called "front-running," or buying shares with insider knowledge that a takeover bid would be launched.

"There was no front-running at all," Noval said. "The fact of life was that from Canadian 88's standpoint and West Central, there never was a bid for Morrison approved or otherwise until the Sunday prior to our bid, nor did we have the bank financing in place until Monday a.m."
Canadian 88 announced its offer on Monday January 13.
He said he believed Morrison was pushing for the investigation as a tactic to buy more time in the takeover battle to solicit higher offers.

Canadian 88's offer expires on Friday and Noval repeated that his offer would not be extended or raised. Canadian 88 has offered C$10 cash, to a maximum cash portion of C$140 million, or 1.5 of its shares for each Morrison share.
However, the firms' stock prices suggest investors are still betting on a higher offer surfacing.
Canadian 88 on Tuesday closed down C$0.55 to C$5.75 in Toronto, placing the share swap at C$8.63. Morrison was down C$0.05 to C$10.30.
